**Problem on 11/09/2026:**

Prior to the first Integration run using Harmony, I got an error that indicated that there was an incorrect matrix columns. I sifter through my data tables to make sure that at least all of sample titles were filled. Turns out one was not it was supposed to be.

Somehow the sample HP0(GSM5494346) was transformed into Healthy-PC1 identity and condition column along with all other clinical variables it should have (Age) is gone. Not only that but this change is only isolated to HP0. All other samples are unaffected.

Solution

# Finally Integration Time

**Run Normalization**

**Run Variable Features**

Ranks Features by number of dataset they are deemed variable. Because the variance of a genes scales non-linearly with the mean expression of each gene, methods will need to isolate heterogeneity using a normalized or standardized metric. Asking: How much more variable a gene is than expected given it's mean expression

Ways to rank features:

1.  Dispersion-Based

Dispersion_i = variance_i / mean_i

2.  Variance Stabilization method (local polynomial Regression)
3.  Pearson Residual Variance

**Select Integration Features:** Ranks features by the number of datasets they are deemed variable. Breaking ties by the median variable features rank across datasets.

```{r}
library(harmony)
```

```{r}
PCa_list <- list(gse181294.obj, gse150692.obj, gse176031.obj, gse141445.obj)
names(PCa_list) <- c("GSE181294", "GSE150692", "GSE176031", "GSE141445")

#clear individual Seurat objects from active RAM
rm(gse181294.obj, 
   gse150692.obj, 
   gse176031.obj, 
   gse141445.obj)

#perform normalization on each individually
#perform scaleData individually
PCa_list <- lapply(X = PCa_list, FUN = function(x){
  #Log Normalize
  x <- NormalizeData(x, 
                     verbose = FALSE,
                      normalization.method = "LogNormalize")
})

#merge the list of Seurat Object
PCa_object <- merge(
  x = PCa_list[[1]],
  y = PCa_list[-1],
  add.cell.ids = names(PCa_list),
  project = "merge_object"
)


#Join Layers
PCa_object <- JoinLayers(PCa_object)
PCa_object <- FindVariableFeatures(PCa_object, selection.method = "vst", nfeatures = 10000)

PCa_object <- ScaleData( PCa_object, features = VariableFeatures(PCa_object))
PCa_object <- RunPCA(PCa_object, npcs = 20, verbose = FALSE)

```

dim(PCa_object@assays$RNA$data)

```{r}
#Harmony: directly give covariates to batch correct on th covariates using the PCA embeddings.

# Run Harmony (corrects batch effects on PCA embedding)
PCa_object_int <- RunHarmony(PCa_object, c("geo_acc", "sampleID", "title"))
rm(PCa_object)

PCa_object_int <- NormalizeData(PCa_object_int, normalization.method = "LogNormalize")

PCa_object_int <- FindVariableFeatures(PCa_object_int, nfeatures = 2000, verbose = FALSE)

PCa_object_int <- ScaleData(PCa_object_int, verbose = FALSE)

PCa_object_int <- RunPCA(PCa_object_int, npcs = 50, verbose = FALSE)
PCa_object_int <- RunUMAP(PCa_object_int, dims = 1:30, reduction = "pca", verbose = FALSE)
PCa_object_int <- FindNeighbors(PCa_object_int, dims = 1:30, verbose = FALSE)
PCa_object_int <- FindClusters(PCa_object_int, resolution = 0.6, verbose = FALSE)


```
